text: For a livestock farm, every cow is a valuable asset.
But information about that animal is often scattered across records, camera footage, and insurance documents.
When something goes wrong, finding the right evidence and taking action can take too long.
Meet VEYRA, an AI-powered platform that connects livestock identity, health observations, and insurance in one place.
Our goal is simple: know every animal, understand its financial value, and protect it with clearer, faster workflows.
We begin at the herd dashboard, where a farm manager can see registered cattle, estimated asset values, insurance status, and alerts.
To add a cow, the operator uploads one guided video showing its nose, teeth, and full body.
VEYRA extracts useful images, then asks a person to confirm the animal's identity.
If the match is unclear, the record stays unconfirmed instead of guessing.
Once confirmed, the cow receives a Digital Livestock Passport.
This page brings together its identity images, age and weight estimates, observation history, and supporting documents.
VEYRA also calculates an estimated value range using the confirmed weight and a selected price per kilogram.
The calculation is transparent, and it is not presented as a guaranteed selling price or insurance payout.
Next, the insurance assistant compares three example policies.
It checks eligibility rules and shows premiums, coverage, exclusions, and possible gaps.
Instead of simply recommending the cheapest option, VEYRA explains the tradeoffs, helping the farm manager make an informed choice.
Once the manager selects a policy, the AI agent prepares an application and a separate premium payment.
Nothing important happens without approval.
The manager checks the details, approves each action, and sees the test provider's response.
This demo uses a sandbox, not real money.
And successful payment does not mean coverage is active until the insurer confirms it.
VEYRA also connects each passport to camera observations.
In this demo, a recorded camera feed shows cattle tracks and their last known locations.
If an identified cow moves noticeably less than expected, VEYRA creates an alert with a timestamp and supporting footage.
This is a reason to inspect the animal, not a medical diagnosis.
The manager can even ask, 'Where was this cow last seen?' and receive an answer based on recorded observations.
If the manager later records an incident, the insurance agent helps prepare a claim.
It gathers the passport, relevant observations, policy details, and available evidence into one checklist.
Missing documents are flagged before submission.
Only after the manager checks the facts and approves does VEYRA send the claim to the simulated insurer, where its status becomes pending assessment.
Every important step leaves an audit trail: who confirmed an identity, which action was approved, and what the provider returned.
If information is uncertain or approval is missing, VEYRA blocks the action.
VEYRA connects animal identity with financial protection.
Know every animal.
Protect every asset.
